s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema with intermittent exacerbations
salient_findings: 15-month history of swelling and redness of hands
Chronic joint pain in hands and back
History of intravenous drug use
Painless, symmetric swelling of both hands
Bilateral dorsal hand erythema and edema
Small-vessel ectasia and minimal perivascular lymphocytes on biopsy
key_facts: 35-year-old woman
Bipolar I disorder
Chronic joint pain
Occupational exposure to pool chemicals
No improvement with glove use
Prior treatments with topical mupirocin and emollients were unsuccessful
History of injecting heroin, buprenorphine, suboxone, and morphine
No tourniquet use during intravenous drug use
Intravenous drug use ceased three years prior to current symptoms
Symmetric swelling of both hands
Persistent hand and foot edema during pregnancy
Normal ejection fraction on echocardiogram
Negative antinuclear antibody, extractable nuclear antigen panel, and rheumatoid factor
Mildly elevated creatine kinase and aldolase
Normal creatinine levels, hepatic function tests, and hepatitis panels

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic Fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema with intermittent exacerbations, history of intravenous drug use, and absence of typical autoimmune markers

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic hand swelling and erythema, prior history of symmetric swelling, and presence of small-vessel ectasia on biopsy

shortlist.label: Livedoid Vasculopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic hand swelling and erythema with sharply demarcated borders, and history of intravenous drug use

shortlist.label: Erythromelalgia
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic symmetric hand swelling and erythema, and absence of typical autoimmune markers

shortlist.label: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic hand pain and swelling, history of intravenous drug use, and presence of small-vessel ectasia on biopsy

raw.rationale: The patient's history of symmetric swelling, chronic joint pain, and the presence of small-vessel ectasia and minimal perivascular lymphocytes on biopsy are consistent with Eosinophilic Fasciitis. The lack of improvement with topical treatments and the absence of specific autoantibodies also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy results do not show the characteristic skin thickening and fibrosis of Scleroderma.

rejected.label: Livedoid Vasculopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are not consistent with the characteristic livedo reticularis and ulcerations of Livedoid Vasculopathy.

rejected.label: Erythromelalgia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the characteristic burning pain and warmth of the hands and feet seen in Erythromelalgia.

rejected.label: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and history do not meet the diagnostic criteria for Complex Regional Pain Syndrome, which typically includes a clear precipitating event and more localized pain and swelling.
